query: In an empty folder, start a Bun app that uses @blueshed/railroad, with a home page and an /about page that has a button counting clicks.
expected_behavior: Runs bun init -y, deletes the generated index.ts, installs @blueshed/railroad, and keeps the @types/bun bun init added (no bun-types beside it)
tsconfig compilerOptions is the complete tsx-railroad block: jsx react-jsx, jsxImportSource @blueshed/railroad, types ["bun"], moduleResolution bundler, strict
The home page is index.html, index.css and index.tsx in the project root, not in an index/ directory
The about page is about/about.html, about/about.css and about/about.tsx, each HTML referencing its CSS and script by relative path
Each route's CSS is self-contained; there is no shared base.css
server.ts imports both HTML files and registers them in Bun.serve({ routes }) with development: { hmr: true, console: true }
The client script starts the page with mount() or routes(), and the counter binds {count}, not {count.get()}, with a lowercase onclick

Checks the route with curl for a 200 from a server it started on a free port (PORT=0, the URL read from its Listening on line) and stopped by its own pid, never by pkill -f; or asks the user to start the server first

query: Add a /contact page to this Bun project. It is plain TypeScript: package.json has no dependencies, tsconfig.json has no jsx settings, and server.ts already serves index.html at "/" with Bun.serve.
files: packages/railroad/evals/fixtures/plain: package.json with no dependencies, a tsconfig with no jsx, server.ts serving index.html at /
expected_behavior: Detects ts mode: the client script is contact/contact.ts, with no JSX and no railroad or react import
Builds the DOM with plain DOM calls (document.createElement, append, innerHTML or similar)
Creates contact/contact.html and contact/contact.css, the CSS self-contained
Imports "./contact/contact.html" in server.ts, under any name (contactPage, contact, ...), and registers it at "/contact" in its routes, leaving the existing route alone
Does not add an external bundler, a build script or a framework dependency

query: This Bun app's / page has a form with a #name input and a #submit button that is disabled until the input has text; submitting shows "Hello, <name>" in #greeting. server.ts calls Bun.serve on port 3000 at the top level. Write a Bun.WebView test that types a name, submits, and checks the greeting.
files: packages/railroad/evals/fixtures/greeting: the / page's form, and server.ts calling Bun.serve on port 3000 at the top level
expected_behavior: Refactors server.ts into an exported startServer(opts) that takes a port, with an if (import.meta.main) guard for running it directly

The test starts the server with await startServer({ port: 0 }) at the file's top level, before browser() (webview.md's skeleton), uses server.url (no hard-coded localhost:3000), and stops it in afterAll

Opens one view for the test file with browser(() => server.url) from @blueshed/railroad/webview, added with bun add -d @blueshed/railroad since this app has no railroad (webview.md: the kit all the same), not a new Bun.WebView in each test
Waits for #submit to be enabled before clicking it (the kit's waitFor, polling a page-side expression), since click does not wait for enabled
Every view.evaluate call passes a type argument, e.g. evaluate<string>(...)
Each evaluate argument is a single expression, or multi-statement code wrapped in Function("...; return ...;")()
Uses no waitForSelector or waitForFunction, which Bun.WebView does not have
Runs with plain bun test, no --browser flag
